$comment: Committed baseline for tests/e2e/mobile/chat-render-perf.spec.ts, captured BEFORE any
of the image/chart rendering work. The spec writes its own run to the gitignored
test-results/; this file is the thing to diff against.
Absolute timings are machine-bound (captured on an Apple Silicon laptop against the
Turbopack dev server) — read the RATIOS, not the milliseconds. The load-bearing
numbers are jsHeapUsedBytes / imageBytes (how far the payload amplifies) and
longTasks.worstMs (what the user feels as a freeze).
Caveat on imageBytes: the seeder encodes full-frame noise, which is the worst case
for a given resolution — a real UI screenshot has flat regions and compresses better.
The perf tier's 72MB across 40 frames is therefore closer to what ~150 real 1568px
screenshots weigh. The amplification ratio is unaffected.
readings: 40 images inline as 72MB of base64 and cost 600MB of JS heap — the same bytes are held by the Dexie row, the Zustand store, the DOM attribute and the decoded bitmap at once.

The robustness tier does not crash on a desktop-class Chromium, but 18s to open, a 9.2s main-thread freeze and an 8.1s scroll frame make it unusable; a real iOS WKWebView (~1-1.5GB per tab) would be OOM-killed well before 1.86GB.

The robust tier's lower heap-per-byte ratio is not an improvement: Chromium is already under memory pressure and evicting decoded bitmaps, which is what the 8s scroll frame is — re-decoding on the way back.
Median scroll frame stays healthy in both tiers (32ms / 23ms). The cost is concentrated in a few catastrophic frames, so a median-based metric would have reported everything as fine.
